title: fastlane-reservedlane-admission-controller-with-proportional-credit-decay
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current tier routing (free/paid/enterprise) aggressively demotes free traffic during quota pressure which causes sharp UX regressions and spiky tail latency when paid traffic bursts. We need a router that: 1) fairly prioritizes paid/enterprise while offering bounded, predictable fast-path access to free users, 2) respects region affinity (route to nearest compatible pool when possible), and 3) gracefully fails over to cheaper model variants without violating SLOs.

Goals: Implement an admission controller that maintains proportional credit shares across tiers with an additive decay that smooths bursts ("proportional credit decay"), a short-lived lease token for reserved lanes to guarantee in-flight requests, and a soft-grace policy for free-tier requests (limited hedged fastpath) that can be revoked under sustained pressure. Router must support policy config per-region and per-plan, pluggable fallback model variants, and observability hooks (per-tenant admission events, reason codes).

Proposed design (high level):
- Token buckets per plan-class with two sub-buckets: reserved (leased guarantees for committed capacity) and fastlane (best-effort, elastic access).
- Proportional decay: on each allocation interval we compute allowed tokens for a plan as (base_share * total_capacity) - decay_factor * recent_overuse, where recent_overuse is an EWMA of the plan's consumption above base. Decay factor is configurable per-plan. This smooths aggressive bursts and prevents immediate complete cutoff.
- Lease tokens: when a paid/enterprise request is admitted into reserved lane we issue a short-lived lease token (TTL ~45s) pinned to the request id to protect associated KV cache allocations. Leases are reaped on completion or TTL expiry.
- Free fastpath hedging: free requests may get temporary fastlane tokens up to a small fractional percentage of total capacity (default 5%). Under pressure, hedging window shrinks using a linear backoff.
- Region affinity: admission decisions prefer same-region pools; if insufficient capacity we evaluate cross-region spill using cost and latency thresholds. Spill uses a conservative penalty multiplier so we prefer local fallbacks first.
- Fallback models: each admitted request includes a model_variant affinity list. In overload, router can downgrade to pre-validated cheaper quantized variants with fallback rules per-plan (e.g., free->gpt-small-quant, paid->gpt-medium-quant). Fallback is only allowed if regression tests pass and model compatibility check succeeds.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong enforcement reduces unpredictability for paid customers but hurts free UX. We chose proportional decay + tiny hedging to balance both.
- Lease tokens add state and bookkeeping cost; TTL tuned to bound state growth.
- Cross-region spill increases tail latency for some requests; we add conservative thresholds and a per-tenant opt-out.

Acceptance criteria (must be strings in list):
- Router admits requests according to proportional-shares under synthetic traffic with plan mix 70% free / 25% paid / 5% enterprise and respects configured fastpath cap (5% default).
- p99 latency for paid and enterprise under a 2x paid burst stays within existing SLO + 15% and success rate >= 99.5%.
- Free-tier fastpath is observed but declines smoothly during prolonged pressure (EWMA and decay working).
- Lease tokens are issued and garbage-collected; peak in-memory lease objects < 5k per region under test burst.
- Fallback to cheaper model variants happens only when compatibility checks pass and regression metric delta < threshold defined in rollout policy.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike: implement simulation harness to model proportional decay and hedging behavior (done 2026-02-26).
2) Server: add admission controller module in router service (prototype branch: feature/fastlane-admission).
3) Runtime integration: hook lease token lifecycle to KV cache allocator and request tracer.
4) Fallback config: extend model catalog with variant affinity lists and compatibility checks.
5) Observability: emit admission.events with reason codes, quotas, and plan snapshots; add console dashboard panels.
6) Rollout: staged in two regions (us-west-2, eu-west-1) behind feature flag and canary traffic split.

Monitoring and metrics: per-plan admitted_tokens, denied_tokens, ewma_overuse, leased_tokens, cross_region_spill_count, fallback_count, admission_latency_ms. Add alerts: paid_p99_latency > SLO*1.15 or paid_success_rate < 99.5% triggers immediate rollback.

Rollout and rollback plan:
- Canary (5% traffic) for 48h in us-west-2; observe metrics and heatmap for per-tenant regressions.
- Increase to 25% if stable for 72h.
- Full region rollout after 7d with conservative ramp.
- Rollback is via feature flag; emergency rollback if paid latency or success thresholds breached.

Notes and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Proportional+Credit+Decay+Router
- Simulation notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/drive_sim_fastlane_spike
comments: 2026-02-26: Spike complete. Simulation shows proportional decay avoids cliff demotion for free tier and keeps paid tail latency bounded (notes in spike notebook). - Aisha
2026-03-01: Design review with PM/Design. PM requested per-tenant opt-out for cross-region spill; added opt-out flag. - Marcus
2026-03-04: Security review scheduled; flagged potential lease token exposure in logs. We will avoid logging raw tokens and only emit token_id hash. - Marcus
2026-03-07: Implementation PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/4821 (prototype admission controller + unit tests). Needs integration tests for KV cache leak scenarios. - Marcus
2026-03-10: Design feedback from Reliability: reduce lease TTL from 60s to 45s and limit per-tenant reserved leases. Updated design accordingly. - Priya (Reliability)
2026-03-12: Integration tests added to CI; found race where lease reaping could drop metrics. Patch pushed to PR with fix. Observability events now include reason_code and plan_snapshot. - Marcus
